craft_notes: Sthāyin: determination over delusion (adhyavasāya = determining; the verse's engine). Sanskrit-first: re-read confirms order (initiation-barrier before determination-triumph) and the resolved asaṃkucita fork carried through. Abhinavagupta frame: jñāna-as-opponent (virodhin) — knowledge argued as enemy-of-ignorance, not lamp-in-dark; śāstra as the only full authorizer (five streams→sixfold→Mālinīvijaya, inexhaustible per UNC). Rows: 9 (twofold catalogue — doubt/wrong-conviction/churning each named; each ignorance named is a bond named), 1 (avikalpāntatā end-weighted ‘thought-free’; sarvasmāt ‘altogether’ closes on totality). Close: ‘frees altogether’. Rejected: smoothing the sextet catalogue — killed: naming IS the refutation; ‘mere thought’ for churning thought — killed: manana-churning is technical. Read aloud: KNOW-ledge FREES — two-FOLD … de-CID-ed SHUN-and-TAKE … PRAC-ticed, KILLS the PER-son-al TOO — THOUGHT-free.

lines: Knowledge frees — opposing bondage-cause ignorance, twofold:
intellect-seated doubt and wrong-conviction, person-seated churning thought —
that last, saṃsāra's root. Initiation may wash the personal —
but needs decided shun-and-take; so deciding knowledge leads,
and practiced, kills the personal too — practice ends thought-free.
Pure knowing only — Lord-spoken scripture frees altogether.
l4.sanskrit_cite: iha jñānaṃ mokṣakāraṇaṃ bandhanimittasya ajñānasya virodhakatvāt dvividhaṃ ca ajñānaṃ buddhigataṃ pauruṣaṃ ca tatra buddhigatam aniścayasvabhāvam viparītaniścayātmakaṃ ca pauruṣam tu vikalpasvabhāvam saṃkucitaprathātmakam tad eva ca mūlakāraṇam saṃsārasya iti vakṣyāmo malanirṇaye tatra pauruṣam ajñānaṃ dīkṣādinā nivartetāpi kiṃ tu dīkṣāpi buddhigate anadhyavasāyātmake ajñāne sati na sambhavati heyopādeyaniścayapūrvakatvāt tattvaśuddhiśivayojanārūpāyāḥ dīkṣāyāḥ iti adhyavasāyaātmakaṃ buddhiniṣṭham eva jñānam pradhānam tad eva ca abhyasyamānaṃ pauruṣam api ajñānaṃ nihanti vikalpasaṃvidabhyāsasya avikalpāntatāparyavasānāt hy ātmā vikalpāsaṃkucitsaṃvitprakāśarūpaḥ śivasvabhāvaḥ iti sarvathā samastavastuniṣṭham samyaṅniścayātmakaṃ jñānam upādeyam tac ca śāstrapūrvakam śāstram ca parameśvarabhāṣitam eva pramāṇam aparaśāstroktānām arthānāṃ tatra vaiviktyena abhyupagamāt tadarthātiriktayuktisiddhanirūpaṇāc ca tena aparāgamoktam jñānam tāvataḥ eva bandhāt vimocakam na sarvasmāt sarvasmāt tu vimocakam parameśvaraśāstram pañcasrotomayam daśāṣṭādaśavasvaṣṭabhedabhinnam tato 'pi sarvasmāt sāram ṣaḍardhaśāstrāṇi tebhyo 'pi mālinīvijayam tadantargataś cārthaḥ saṃkalayya aśakyo nirūpayitum na ca anirūpitavastutattvasya muktatvam mocakatvam vā śuddhasya jñānasyaiva tathārūpatvāt iti svabhyastajñānamūlatvāt parapuruṣārthasya tatsiddhaye idam ārabhyate ajñānaṃ kila bandhahetuḥ uditaḥ śāstre malaṃ tat smṛtam pūrṇajñānakalodaye tad akhilam nirmūlatāṃ gacchati dhvastāśeṣamalātmasaṃvidudaye mokṣaḥ ca tena amunā śāstreṇa prakaṭīkaromi nikhilam yaj jñeyatattvam bhavet

reads_against.argmap: What liberates, and by what authority? → Determination-knowledge (śāstra-grounded) removes both ignorances; the Lord's scripture alone fully frees; its essence-chain ends in the Mālinīvijaya, whose content no gathering exhausts.
c1_essence: Knowledge frees as opponent of bondage-cause ignorance, twofold: doubt-natured and wrong-conviction-natured in the intellect, thought-natured and contracted in the person — root of saṃsāra; initiation washes the personal but needs prior shun-and-take determination, impossible while intellect cannot decide; hence determinative intellect-dwelling knowledge is principal, and practiced kills the personal too, ending in thought-free; only Lord-spoken scripture fully authorizes and fully frees, five streams to sixfold books to inexhaustible Mālinīvijaya.
